messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'obsidian-health-pool' (tenant: ObsidianHealth) reports GPU saturation and queue growth above 95% for >3m. Pager sent to eng-sre on-call. https://alerts.redwood.prod/5032109876 :rotating_light:

simon: on it, paging in the oncall rotation. grabbing metrics now.

simon: GPU util 99%, queue=412, p99 latency spiking, backpressure kicking in. tenant traffic dominant (~82% of pool).

amy: pinging runtime team — can we isolate tenant requests or trigger immediate burst?

incident-bot: AUTOSCALER: burst quota available = 2 nodes (30min). Current reserved = 0. cost impact estimate ~+$12k/hr if used.

raj: customer success on call with ObsidianHealth. they're seeing timeouts on their production /generate endpoints. asking for ETA on mitigation.

eve: quick options: 1) enable burst (adds 2 nodes) 2) throttle tenant concurrency 3) fail open to smaller model variant 4) live-migrate some other tenants out (manual). Which to prioritize?

simon: immediate priority = restore customer SLA. recommend burst + reduce their concurrency by 50% and enable fallback model for long requests. do we have approval from eng-sre lead?

tom: I can authorize emergency burst for up to 30m per on-call playbook, cc @simon. confirm we track cost and notify sales/finance. :white_check_mark:

amy: running command to enable burst:
```
redwoodctl pools burst enable --pool obsidian-health-pool --nodes 2 --duration 30m --reason "emergency tenant saturation"
```
Executed, waiting for nodes to register.

incident-bot: ACTION: burst enable accepted by tom. Nodes provisioning (ETA ~1.5m).

simon: reducing tenant concurrency policy (in-flight tokens) for ObsidianHealth to 0.5x via feature-flag.
```
redwoodctl tenant update --tenant obsidian-health --concurrency-multiplier 0.5
```
Applied.

raj: told ObsidianHealth support that we're enabling emergency capacity + throttling to stabilize; they asked to keep them updated every 10m.

eve: also enabling model fallback for long-running requests (>1.5s). route heavy requests to `redwood-small-q4` with KV-cache warmer.
```
redwoodctl routing set --tenant obsidian-health --fallback-model redwood-small-q4 --threshold 1.5s
```
Done.

incident-bot: Nodes registered. Pool capacity increased by 2 nodes. GPU util falling to 76% after 45s. queue=98 -> 34. p95 latency trending down.

simon: confirm from runtime: slow requests still exist but rate has halved. we're within SLA band now. keeping burst active for 30m, monitor.

tom: please capture cost delta and update ticket ENG-5032 with timeline and commands executed. I'll notify finance & AMs.

amy: quick note: we saw a single job pattern from ObsidianHealth with very high concurrency spikes from a batch job at :00 minute. recommend they add rate-limits on their side. raj, can you escalate to their SRE?

raj: on it, I told them to disable the scheduled batch for now and move to staggered ramp. customer agreed to postpone next run.

incident-bot: REMINDER: burst will auto-expire at +30m from enable (503210(?) + 1800s). Manual extend requires 2 approvers.

eve: monitoring for regressions: traces show cache misses for big prompts. warming KV-cache for fallback model now.

simon: switching incident channel to a short handoff at +20m: @amy will lead mitigation, I'll do post-incident analysis and hand off on-call.

tom: agreed. also schedule an immediate follow-up call with ObsidianHealth leadership after stabilization.

amy: +20m update: metrics stable, queue <10, p99 below SLA. burst still on with 10m remaining.

raj: customer confirms degradation subsided. thanks team. they requested confirmation when burst ends.

simon: will monitor until burst expires. action items: (1) postmortem draft (owner: simon) (2) recommend tenant-level autoscale config (owner: eve) (3) account-level rate-limits guidance (owner: raj) (4) cost review (owner: tom).

incident-bot: BURST EXPIRED: burst duration ended, nodes drained successfully, pool back to baseline. final metrics: peak GPU util 99%, time to stabilize 4m, cost estimate +$9.8k for burst window.

simon: closing incident thread. will open postmortem in ~2h, include timeline & customer communication. thanks all. :pray:
